nodes.label: CACNA1A
nodes.summary_plain: Builds pore-forming alpha-1A subunit of P/Q-type calcium channel essential for neurotransmitter release.

nodes.label: ATP1A2
nodes.summary_plain: Encodes sodium/potassium ATPase alpha-2 subunit that regulates glial ion balance and glutamate clearance.

nodes.label: SCN1A
nodes.summary_plain: Encodes voltage-gated sodium channel Nav1.1 critical for GABAergic inhibitory interneuron firing.

nodes.label: KCNA1
nodes.summary_plain: Encodes voltage-gated potassium channel Kv1.1 controlling repolarization in cerebellar basket cells.

nodes.label: CACNB4
nodes.summary_plain: Encodes calcium channel beta-4 auxiliary subunit that modulates Cav2.1 and Cav2.2 trafficking.

nodes.label: SLC1A3
nodes.summary_plain: Encodes excitatory amino acid transporter 1 (GLAST) clearing synaptic glutamate in Bergmann glia.

nodes.label: ATXN1
nodes.summary_plain: Encodes ataxin-1; CAG repeat expansion causes cerebellar Purkinje cell neurodegeneration.

nodes.label: ATXN2
nodes.summary_plain: Encodes ataxin-2; polyglutamine expansion impairs RNA metabolism and translation.

nodes.label: ATXN3
nodes.summary_plain: Encodes ataxin-3 deubiquitinase; polyQ expansion leads to toxic protein aggregates.

nodes.label: ATXN7
nodes.summary_plain: Encodes ataxin-7 subunit of STAGA complex; polyQ expansion causes ataxia with macular degeneration.

nodes.label: CACNA1B
nodes.summary_plain: Encodes N-type voltage-gated calcium channel pore subunit closely related to Cav2.1.

nodes.label: CACNA1E
nodes.summary_plain: Encodes R-type calcium channel alpha-1E subunit implicated in early infantile epileptic encephalopathy.

nodes.label: Episodic Ataxia Type 2
nodes.summary_plain: Recurrent attacks of unsteadiness, vertigo, and slurred speech lasting hours, triggered by stress or exertion.

nodes.label: Familial Hemiplegic Migraine Type 1
nodes.summary_plain: Severe migraines accompanied by temporary weakness on one side of the body and visual disturbances.

nodes.label: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 6
nodes.summary_plain: Gradual, progressive loss of balance and coordination beginning in mid-to-late adulthood.

nodes.label: Developmental and Epileptic Encephalopathy 42
nodes.summary_plain: Severe early-onset seizures, developmental arrest or regression, and muscle tone abnormalities.

nodes.label: Episodic Ataxia Type 1
nodes.summary_plain: Brief attacks of ataxia and persistent muscle rippling (myokymia) caused by potassium channel defects.

nodes.label: Familial Hemiplegic Migraine Type 2
nodes.summary_plain: Migraines with motor weakness caused by pump defects that disrupt brain potassium and glutamate removal.

nodes.label: Familial Hemiplegic Migraine Type 3
nodes.summary_plain: Migraines with transient motor weakness caused by gain-of-function sodium channel Nav1.1 variants.

nodes.label: Episodic Ataxia Type 5
nodes.summary_plain: Paroxysmal ataxia episodes caused by mutations in the calcium channel beta-4 auxiliary subunit.

nodes.label: Episodic Ataxia Type 6
nodes.summary_plain: Episodic ataxia with seizures and hemiplegia caused by impaired glial glutamate uptake transporter.

nodes.label: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 1
nodes.summary_plain: Progressive neurodegenerative cerebellar ataxia caused by CAG polyglutamine expansion in ATXN1.

nodes.label: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 2
nodes.summary_plain: Autosomal dominant progressive ataxia with slow saccadic eye movements caused by ATXN2 CAG expansion.

nodes.label: Machado-Joseph Disease (SCA3)
nodes.summary_plain: Progressive cerebellar ataxia with spasticity and peripheral neuropathy caused by ATXN3 CAG expansion.

nodes.label: Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 7
nodes.summary_plain: Adult-onset progressive cerebellar ataxia accompanied by progressive cone-rod retinal dystrophy.

nodes.label: Dravet Syndrome
nodes.summary_plain: Severe childhood epilepsy syndrome commonly triggered by fever and linked to SCN1A channel loss of function.

nodes.label: Cav2.1 Loss of Function
nodes.summary_plain: Decreased calcium influx at presynaptic terminals impairs neurotransmitter release in cerebellar circuits.

nodes.label: Cav2.1 Gain of Function
nodes.summary_plain: Increased calcium influx at lower voltages facilitates cortical spreading depression and migraine aura.

nodes.label: Polyglutamine CAG Expansion Toxicity
nodes.summary_plain: Abnormally long glutamine tracts cause protein misfolding, aggregate buildup, and Purkinje cell death.

nodes.label: Cortical Spreading Depression
nodes.summary_plain: A slow wave of cellular depolarization in the cerebral cortex that triggers migraine aura and headache.

nodes.label: Purkinje Cell Pacemaking Instability
nodes.summary_plain: Loss of regular high-frequency firing in Purkinje cells disrupts motor coordination outputs.

nodes.label: Glutamate Clearance Impairment
nodes.summary_plain: Failure of astrocytic pumps or transporters leads to excessive extracellular glutamate and hyperexcitability.

nodes.label: CACNA1A c.575G>A (p.Arg192Gln)
nodes.summary_plain: Well-characterized gain-of-function missense variant causing familial hemiplegic migraine type 1.

nodes.label: CACNA1A c.653C>T (p.Ser218Leu)
nodes.summary_plain: Severe gain-of-function mutation causing hemiplegic migraine, delayed cerebral edema, and coma after mild trauma.

nodes.label: CACNA1A c.1994C>T (p.Thr665Met) (legacy T666M)
nodes.summary_plain: Pore region gain-of-function mutation causing severe familial hemiplegic migraine type 1.

nodes.label: CACNA1A c.4633C>T (p.Arg1545Ter)
nodes.summary_plain: Nonsense truncating mutation causing loss of Cav2.1 channel function and episodic ataxia type 2.

nodes.label: CACNA1A c.4979G>A (p.Arg1660His) (legacy R1666H)
nodes.summary_plain: Recurrent de novo missense variant causing severe developmental delay and early epileptic encephalopathy.

nodes.label: Ataxia
nodes.summary_plain: Lack of voluntary coordination of muscle movements including gait and limb control.

nodes.label: Episodic ataxia
nodes.summary_plain: Sudden recurring episodes of unsteady balance and clumsiness.

nodes.label: Nystagmus
nodes.summary_plain: Rhythmic, involuntary movements of the eyes, often triggered by looking sideways.

nodes.label: Dysarthria
nodes.summary_plain: Difficulty speaking clearly due to impaired coordination of speech muscles.

nodes.label: Migraine with aura
nodes.summary_plain: Severe headaches preceded by sensory or visual changes such as flashing lights.

nodes.label: Hemiplegia
nodes.summary_plain: Temporary or permanent paralysis affecting one side of the body.

nodes.label: Seizure
nodes.summary_plain: Sudden, uncontrolled electrical disturbance in the brain altering behavior or awareness.

nodes.label: Cerebral edema
nodes.summary_plain: Accumulation of fluid in brain tissues that can cause pressure and coma after head trauma.

nodes.label: Global developmental delay
nodes.summary_plain: Delayed attainment of motor, language, cognitive, or social milestones in childhood.

nodes.label: Vertigo
nodes.summary_plain: Sensation that the room is spinning or moving when standing or sitting.

nodes.label: Hypotonia
nodes.summary_plain: Decreased muscle tone causing floppiness and delayed motor development.

nodes.label: Dystonia
nodes.summary_plain: Twisting, repetitive movements or abnormal postures caused by involuntary muscle contractions.

nodes.label: Spasticity
nodes.summary_plain: Condition in which muscles stiffen or tighten, preventing normal fluid movement.

nodes.label: Cerebellar atrophy
nodes.summary_plain: Progressive loss of tissue in the cerebellum visible on brain MRI scans.

nodes.label: Delayed speech and language development
nodes.summary_plain: Late development of speech and expressive language skills in early childhood.

nodes.label: Progressive cerebellar ataxia
nodes.summary_plain: Slowly worsening lack of coordination and balance over years.

nodes.label: Headache
nodes.summary_plain: Pain in the head or upper neck commonly accompanying migraine or paroxysmal neurological attacks.

nodes.label: Acetazolamide
nodes.summary_plain: Carbonic anhydrase inhibitor reducing episodic ataxia attacks by modifying pH and extracellular ions.

nodes.label: 4-Aminopyridine
nodes.summary_plain: Potassium channel blocker that restores regular pacemaking in Purkinje cells to prevent ataxia attacks.

nodes.label: Verapamil
nodes.summary_plain: L-type calcium channel blocker used off-label for prophylaxis against hemiplegic migraine attacks.

nodes.label: Flunarizine
nodes.summary_plain: Dual calcium and sodium antagonist used internationally for migraine prophylaxis.

nodes.label: Troriluzole
nodes.summary_plain: Prodrug of riluzole designed to enhance glial glutamate uptake and reduce cerebellar excitotoxicity.

nodes.label: Sodium Valproate
nodes.summary_plain: Broad-spectrum anticonvulsant and migraine preventive agent enhancing GABA neurotransmission.

nodes.label: Lamotrigine
nodes.summary_plain: Voltage-gated sodium channel blocker used for seizure prevention and migraine aura prophylaxis.

nodes.label: Levetiracetam
nodes.summary_plain: Antiepileptic drug binding SV2A vesicle protein to moderate neurotransmitter release in refractory seizures.

nodes.label: Topiramate
nodes.summary_plain: Broad-acting channel modulator and mild carbonic anhydrase inhibitor used for migraine prevention.

nodes.label: CACNA1A Foundation
nodes.summary_plain: Leading international patient advocacy organization supporting families and funding CACNA1A research.

nodes.label: National Ataxia Foundation
nodes.summary_plain: US advocacy group dedicated to accelerating treatments and cure for all forms of ataxia including EA2 and SCA6.

nodes.label: Ataxia UK
nodes.summary_plain: UK charity providing support, clinical guidelines, and research funding for cerebellar ataxias.

nodes.label: Euro-Ataxia
nodes.summary_plain: Federation of national ataxia patient associations in Europe coordinating transnational advocacy.

nodes.label: Ataxia Global Initiative
nodes.summary_plain: Worldwide platform uniting clinicians, patient advocates, and industry for trial readiness in ataxias.

nodes.label: Rare Epilepsy Network
nodes.summary_plain: Collaborative network connecting rare developmental and epileptic encephalopathy communities.

nodes.label: Dravet Syndrome Foundation
nodes.summary_plain: Patient organization funding channelopathy research and family support for SCN1A-related seizures.

nodes.label: The Migraine Trust
nodes.summary_plain: UK charity funding research, promoting awareness, and providing support for severe migraine conditions.

nodes.label: CACNA1A Connect (patient registry)
nodes.summary_plain: Registry where families share medical history so research reflects real life.

nodes.label: CACNA1A Natural History Study (Chung Lab, Boston Children's Hospital)
nodes.summary_plain: Long-term study following people with CACNA1A conditions to learn how symptoms change over time.

nodes.label: Tottering Mouse Model (Cacna1a tg)
nodes.summary_plain: Recessive mouse model with Cacna1a mutation exhibiting episodic dystonia, absence seizures, and mild ataxia.

nodes.label: Leaner Mouse Model (Cacna1a tg-la)
nodes.summary_plain: Severe loss-of-function Cacna1a splicing mutant mouse showing cerebellar granule and Purkinje neurodegeneration.

nodes.label: Rolling Nagoya Mouse Model (Cacna1a tg-rol)
nodes.summary_plain: Spontaneous mouse mutant with reduced Cav2.1 channel activity displaying severe motor ataxia.

nodes.label: R192Q Knock-in Mouse Model
nodes.summary_plain: Gain-of-function knock-in mouse displaying lowered threshold and accelerated propagation of cortical spreading depression.

nodes.label: S218L Knock-in Mouse Model
nodes.summary_plain: Severe gain-of-function model displaying susceptibility to lethal seizures and brain edema after mild concussive trigger.

nodes.label: 4-Aminopyridine in Episodic Ataxia Type 2
nodes.summary_plain: Planned placebo-controlled trial of 4-aminopyridine in episodic ataxia type 2. It was withdrawn before enrolling.

nodes.label: Troriluzole in Adult Participants With Spinocerebellar Ataxia
nodes.summary_plain: Phase 3 clinical trial testing troriluzole efficacy in patients with spinocerebellar ataxias including SCA6.

nodes.label: Natural History Study of and Genetic Modifiers in Spinocerebellar Ataxias
nodes.summary_plain: Longitudinal natural history study by the Clinical Research Consortium for SCAs.

nodes.label: Arn M.J.M. van den Maagdenberg
nodes.summary_plain: Professor at Leiden University Medical Center; pioneering investigator bridging FHM1, EA2, and Cav2.1 channel biology.

nodes.label: Joanna C. Jen
nodes.summary_plain: Professor of Neurology at Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai; international authority on Episodic Ataxia 2 and neurogenetics.

nodes.label: Michael Strupp
nodes.summary_plain: Professor of Neurology at LMU Munich; pioneered 4-aminopyridine as medical therapy for episodic ataxia and cerebellar dysfunction.

nodes.label: Christopher M. Gomez
nodes.summary_plain: Professor at University of Chicago; discovered CACNA1A bicistronic expression of alpha1ACT driving SCA6 pathology.

nodes.label: Wendy K. Chung
nodes.summary_plain: Chief of Pediatrics at Boston Children's / Harvard; principal investigator of the CACNA1A natural history study.

nodes.label: Daniela Pietrobon
nodes.summary_plain: Professor of Physiology at University of Padua; leading expert on biophysical gating mechanisms of Cav2.1 mutants in migraine.

nodes.label: Robert W. Baloh
nodes.summary_plain: Emeritus Professor of Neurology at UCLA; clinical pioneer who characterized episodic ataxia types and vestibulocerebellar disorders.

nodes.label: Thomas Klockgether
nodes.summary_plain: Director at DZNE Bonn; international leader of the EUROSCA natural history consortium in degenerative ataxias.

nodes.label: Stefan M. Pulst
nodes.summary_plain: Chair of Neurology at University of Utah; leader in spinocerebellar ataxia genetics, Purkinje cell channelopathy, and antisense therapies.

nodes.label: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS)
nodes.summary_plain: US federal institute funding biomedical research on the nervous system, channelopathies, and rare neurogenetic diseases.

nodes.label: Chan Zuckerberg Initiative Rare As One
nodes.summary_plain: Philanthropic foundation providing grant funding and organizational capacity to rare disease patient communities.

nodes.label: European Joint Programme on Rare Diseases (EJP RD)
nodes.summary_plain: European research consortium funding transnational collaborative research and registries for rare diseases.

nodes.label: Ophoff et al. 1996 (Cell)
nodes.summary_plain: Landmark paper discovering that CACNA1A mutations cause both familial hemiplegic migraine and episodic ataxia type-2.

nodes.label: Zhuchenko et al. 1997 (Nat Genet)
nodes.summary_plain: Discovered that small CAG repeat expansions in CACNA1A cause spinocerebellar ataxia type 6.

nodes.label: van den Maagdenberg et al. 2004 (Neuron)
nodes.summary_plain: Engineered human Cacna1a R192Q knock-in migraine mouse model displaying increased cortical spreading depression.

nodes.label: Strupp et al. 2004 (Neurology)
nodes.summary_plain: Demonstrated successful clinical treatment of episodic ataxia type 2 attacks with potassium channel blocker 4-aminopyridine.

nodes.label: Du et al. 2013 (Cell)
nodes.summary_plain: Discovered that a second cistron within CACNA1A encodes alpha1ACT transcription factor driving SCA6 neurodegeneration.

nodes.label: Indelicato & Boesch 2026 (Cerebellum)
nodes.summary_plain: Demonstrated genotype and age-at-onset drive vermian cerebellar atrophy in CACNA1A-related ataxias.

nodes.label: Kessi et al. 2023 (Front Mol Neurosci)
nodes.summary_plain: Genotype-phenotype review of CACNA1A-related childhood neurodevelopmental disorders and epileptic encephalopathy.

nodes.label: Tottene et al. 2009 (Neuron)
nodes.summary_plain: Demonstrated that enhanced synaptic glutamate release underlies spreading depression susceptibility in Cav2.1 knock-in mice.

nodes.label: De Fusco et al. 2003 (Nat Genet)
nodes.summary_plain: Identified haploinsufficiency of ATP1A2 encoding Na+/K+ pump alpha-2 subunit in familial hemiplegic migraine type 2.

nodes.label: Dichgans et al. 2005 (Lancet)
nodes.summary_plain: Identified mutation in neuronal voltage-gated sodium channel SCN1A in familial hemiplegic migraine.

nodes.label: Browne et al. 1994 (Nat Genet)
nodes.summary_plain: Proved episodic ataxia/myokymia syndrome is caused by mutations in voltage-gated potassium channel KCNA1.

nodes.label: Jen et al. 2005 (Neurology)
nodes.summary_plain: Discovered that mutation in glutamate transporter EAAT1 (SLC1A3) causes episodic ataxia, hemiplegia, and seizures.

nodes.label: Jacobi et al. 2015 (Lancet Neurol)
nodes.summary_plain: Long-term prospective disease progression study of spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, and 6 in EUROSCA cohort.

nodes.label: Pivotal Study of N-acetyl-L-leucine for CACNA1A
nodes.summary_plain: Phase 3 trial now recruiting people with CACNA1A conditions (SCA6, EA2, FHM1) to test N-acetyl-L-leucine against placebo.

evidence.quote: Episodic ataxia type 2 is caused by heterozygous mutation in CACNA1A.
Familial hemiplegic migraine-1 is caused by heterozygous missense mutation in CACNA1A.
SCA6 is caused by heterozygous expansion of a CAG repeat in the CACNA1A gene.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy-42 is caused by heterozygous de novo mutation in the CACNA1A gene.
FHM2 is caused by heterozygous mutation in the ATP1A2 gene.
FHM3 is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SCN1A gene.
Dravet syndrome is caused by heterozygous loss of function mutation in SCN1A.
Episodic ataxia type 1 is caused by heterozygous mutation in KCNA1.
Episodic ataxia type 5 is caused by heterozygous mutation in CACNB4.
Episodic ataxia type 6 is caused by heterozygous mutation in SLC1A3.
SCA1 is caused by heterozygous expansion of a CAG trinucleotide repeat in ATXN1.
SCA2 is caused by heterozygous expansion of a CAG trinucleotide repeat in ATXN2.
SCA3 is caused by heterozygous expansion of a CAG repeat in ATXN3.
SCA7 is caused by heterozygous expansion of a CAG trinucleotide repeat in ATXN7.
NM_001127221.2:c.574C>T (p.Arg192Gln) Pathogenic for Familial hemiplegic migraine 1.
NM_001127221.2:c.653C>T (p.Ser218Leu) Pathogenic for Familial hemiplegic migraine 1.
NM_001127221.2:c.1997C>T (p.Thr666Met) Pathogenic for Familial hemiplegic migraine 1.
NM_001127221.2:c.4072C>T (p.Arg1358Ter) Pathogenic for Episodic ataxia type 2.
NM_001127221.2:c.4997G>A (p.Arg1666His) Pathogenic for CACNA1A-related epileptic encephalopathy.
R192Q mutation causes a gain of function with shift of activation to more hyperpolarized potentials.
S218L mutation causes massive increase in open probability and hyperpolarizing activation shift.
Pore mutations like T666M cause enhanced calcium influx at single channel level.
Truncation mutations in EA2 result in loss of functional Cav2.1 channel expression.
R192Q identified in multiple families with classic FHM1.
S218L causes severe FHM1 with trauma-induced cerebral edema and coma.
T666M causes typical and severe hemiplegic migraine type 1.
Premature termination codon R1358Ter causes Episodic Ataxia type 2.
R1666H confirmed de novo in children with DEE42.
Loss-of-function mutations and haploinsufficiency of Cav2.1 underlie episodic ataxia type 2.
Cav2.1 gain of function facilitates cortical spreading depression in hemiplegic migraine.
CAG expansion in CACNA1A bicistronic alpha1ACT fragment mediates Purkinje cell neurotoxicity in SCA6.
Polyglutamine repeat expansion causes Purkinje cell degeneration in SCA1.
Polyglutamine repeat expansion in ataxin-2 causes neurodegeneration in SCA2.
Polyglutamine tract expansion in ataxin-3 produces cytotoxic aggregates in SCA3.
Expanded polyQ tract in ataxin-7 causes cerebellar and retinal neurodegeneration in SCA7.
Enhanced presynaptic Ca2+ influx via mutated Cav2.1 channels facilitates induction of cortical spreading depression.
Decreased P/Q current destabilizes precision pacemaking in cerebellar Purkinje neurons.
Impaired astrocytic K+ and glutamate clearance lowers threshold for cortical spreading depression in FHM2.
EAAT1 glutamate transporter dysfunction impairs synaptic clearance driving EA6 episodes.
Both CACNA1A and ATP1A2 cause familial hemiplegic migraine by promoting cortical spreading depression.
SCN1A and CACNA1A encode voltage-gated ion channels causing hemiplegic migraine through neuronal hyperexcitability.
KCNA1 and CACNA1A are cerebellar ion channels causing episodic ataxias with responsive episodes.
CACNB4 encodes the beta-4 auxiliary subunit directly interacting with CACNA1A alpha-1A subunit.
Mutations in SLC1A3 cause EA6 with overlapping clinical features of episodic ataxia and hemiplegia.
ATXN1 and CACNA1A share polyglutamine CAG expansion mechanism driving cerebellar Purkinje degeneration.
ATXN2 and CACNA1A both manifest pathogenic CAG trinucleotide repeat expansions in hereditary ataxia.
ATXN3 and CACNA1A share autosomal dominant CAG trinucleotide expansion pathology.
ATXN7 and CACNA1A both cause dominant polyglutamine cerebellar ataxias.
CACNA1B (Cav2.2) and CACNA1A (Cav2.1) are paralogous presynaptic calcium channels sharing gating homology.
CACNA1E (Cav2.3) and CACNA1A both cause infantile epileptic encephalopathies when mutated.
Episodic ataxia is the hallmark cardinal phenotype of EA2.
Interictal nystagmus (gaze-evoked or downbeat) is highly prevalent in EA2.
Dysarthria occurs during attacks and in interictal stages of EA2.
Vertigo is a frequent precipitating symptom of episodic ataxia attacks.
Baseline progressive cerebellar ataxia develops in older adults with EA2.
Cerebellar vermian atrophy is observed on MRI in longstanding EA2.
Dystonia and dystonic posturing can accompany episodic ataxia attacks.
Migraine with aura is defining manifestation of FHM1.
Transient motor hemiplegia during migraine aura defines hemiplegic migraine.
Severe FHM1 cases (e.g. S218L) exhibit acute cerebral edema following minor head trauma.
Epileptic seizures occur in severe manifestations of hemiplegic migraine.
Pulsating severe headache is the principal symptom of FHM1 episodes.
Permanent cerebellar signs including nystagmus occur in families with FHM1.
Progressive cerebellar ataxia is the core feature of SCA6.
Progressive course of cerebellar unsteadiness over decades in SCA6.
Downbeat nystagmus is a frequent early ocular sign in SCA6.
Progressive scanning dysarthria accompanies gait ataxia in SCA6.
Marked cerebellar vermis and hemispheric atrophy on brain neuroimaging in SCA6.
Mild pyramidal spasticity and brisk reflexes can develop late in SCA6 course.
Intractable infantile epileptic seizures characterize DEE42.
Severe global developmental delay and intellectual disability in DEE42.
Congenital hypotonia is frequently the initial presentation of DEE42.
Severe speech and language impairment is universal in DEE42 children.
Non-progressive congenital cerebellar ataxia occurs in CACNA1A encephalopathy.
Brief episodes of ataxia lasting seconds to minutes define EA1.
Hemiplegia during migraine attacks characterizes FHM2.
Seizures can accompany hemiplegic migraine episodes in FHM2.
Transient hemiparesis or hemiplegia during aura in FHM3.
Febrile and unprovoked refractory seizures characterize Dravet syndrome.
Developmental plateauing and regression in Dravet syndrome.
Cerebellar ataxia is the presenting symptom in SCA1.
Prominent spasticity and hyperreflexia develop in SCA1.
Progressive cerebellar ataxia is universal in SCA2.
Gait and limb ataxia are cardinal features of SCA3.
Severe progressive ataxia manifests in SCA7 patients.
Acetazolamide is standard first-line therapy dramatically decreasing attack frequency in EA2.
Acetazolamide partially controls attacks in some patients with episodic ataxia type 1.
Acetazolamide shows variable response in FHM1; some patients report benefit while others show lack of efficacy.
Carbonic anhydrase inhibition aborts episodic ataxia attacks.
4-Aminopyridine significantly reduces attack frequency in patients with episodic ataxia type 2.
Potassium channel blockade prevents paroxysmal ataxia attacks.
4-Aminopyridine suppresses downbeat nystagmus by restoring cerebellar Purkinje cell inhibition.
Calcium channel blockers such as verapamil are used off-label for prophylaxis in FHM.
Flunarizine reduces frequency and severity of hemiplegic migraine attacks.
Lamotrigine reduces aura frequency and motor episodes in hemiplegic migraine.
Topiramate is commonly employed for preventive therapy in hemiplegic migraine.
Phase 3 trial evaluating whether troriluzole slows disease progression in SCA genotypes including SCA6.
Troriluzole trial cohort includes genetically confirmed SCA1 participants.
Troriluzole trial cohort includes genetically confirmed SCA2 participants.

Sodium valproate is an established anti-seizure medication for childhood epileptic spasms.
